claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **name and date of birth of the child or children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He just turned 19 in December, so he's 19 years old now. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you're asking about your son Alex, who is now 19 years old.

Before I can assess his eligibility, I need to ask: **Is Alex in full-time education or an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

One more question to complete my assessment: **Does Alex have any disability or health condition that would prevent him from working?** This includes whether he's registered as disabled or receiving any disability-related benefits.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't have any disability or health condition. He's healthy, though he has been in hospital recently - he's been there for a few months now actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a follow-up question about his recent hospital stay:

**Is Alex receiving treatment in hospital as an inpatient, and if so, is he expected to remain there for an extended period, or is this a temporary admission while he continues his studies?**

This matters because there are specific rules about Child Benefit eligibility when a young person is in hospital care.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's been an inpatient at the hospital - it's been about 11 weeks now. He's still doing his A-level work when he can, but he's in the hospital ward for treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important detail. I have one more clarification question:

**How much longer is Alex expected to remain in the hospital as an inpatient?** Is there an expected discharge date, or is his length of stay still uncertain?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're not entirely sure yet - the doctors haven't given us a firm discharge date. It could be another week or two, or it might be a bit longer depending on how his treatment goes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review the situation carefully based on the Child Benefit rules:

- Alex is 19 years old
- He is in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- He has no disability
- He is currently an inpatient in hospital and has been for approximately 11 weeks

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, when a young person is in hospital as an inpatient, there are specific time limits on how long Child Benefit can continue to be paid. The rules state that Child Benefit can be paid for up to 12 weeks while a young person is an inpatient in hospital. After 12 weeks, eligibility ends.

Since Alex has already been hospitalized for 11 weeks, he is approaching this 12-week limit. However, as he has not yet reached the 12-week threshold, he would currently still be eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Yes, you are currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

- **Age**: Alex is 19, which is within the eligible age range (under 20)
- **Full-time education**: He is studying for his A-levels, which qualifies him
- **Hospital stay**: While Alex is an inpatient, the rules allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 12 weeks. Since he has been hospitalized for about 11 weeks, he is still within this eligible period

**Important note**: Once Alex reaches 12 weeks of continuous hospitalization, his eligibility will end unless he is discharged before that point. I'd recommend contacting HMRC if his hospitalization extends beyond 12 weeks to discuss any changes to his circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
